visible_bad_hover: مُوسَىٰ shown split as a مُـ prefix plus a وسى stem; ٱلَّذِى shown split as the definite article plus a noun stem
corrected_hover_or_pending_reason: مُوسَىٰ is one qg-proper-noun segment; ٱلَّذِى is one qg-relative segment
what_failed: The transclusion source-selector scored candidate analyses by (fallback-free, then MAXIMUM segment count), so an over-segmented minority analysis out-ranked the correct single-segment majority that already existed in the whitelist (Musa proper-noun 9/15, alladhi relative 34/48). Mechanical structural gates passed both; only the sarf/nahw review caught it.
sarf_lesson: An aʿlam (proper noun) such as مُوسَىٰ is jamid with no derivational mu- prefix; a frozen relative pronoun such as ٱلَّذِى is mabni and its lam is not the separable definite article. Neither word decomposes into segments.
nahw_lesson: مُوسَىٰ carries a muqaddar (estimated) case ending because it is maqsur, a signature of a frozen aʿlam rather than a derived participle; ٱلَّذِى is mabni ala s-sukun standing in the place of iʿrab as a naʿt. Both are single indivisible units.
learner_explanation: Some words look like they begin with a prefix (like مُـ) or with 'the' (الـ), but are really one solid word. مُوسَىٰ (Moses) and ٱلَّذِى (the one who / which) are each a single piece — do not cut them apart.
drill_prompt: For مُوسَىٰ and for ٱلَّذِى decide: one segment or two, and give the single grammatical class of each.
